question.text: Liquids <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> are at <math> <mrow> <mtext>30</mtext><msup> <mtext> </mtext> <mi>o</mi> </msup> <mtext>C</mtext></mrow> </math> and <math> <mrow> <mtext>20</mtext><msup> <mtext> </mtext> <mi>o</mi> </msup> <mtext>C</mtext></mrow> </math>, respectively. When mixed in equal masses, the temperature of the mixture is found to be <math> <mrow> <mtext>26</mtext><msup> <mtext> </mtext> <mi>o</mi> </msup> <mtext>C</mtext></mrow> </math>, The specific heats of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> are in the ratio of <math> <mrow> <mi>m</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow> </math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> are integers, then find minimum value of <math> <mrow> <mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>.

solution.text:
At thermal equilibrium

heat rejected by one liquid = heat accepted by other liquid

msA30–26=msB26–20

⇒4sA=6sB

∴ sAsB=64=32 = m n ⇒m+n=3+2=5
